text: The applicants are former policemen.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants were all involved in the conflict-resolution and peace-keeping operation in the zone of the armed Ossetian-Ingush conflict in October and November 1992.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a consequence of their involvement in the conflict-resolution and peace-keeping operation in the zone of the armed Ossetian-Ingush conflict, the applicants were entitled to certain social payments.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants sued the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) for social-payments arrears.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
A. Proceedings in respect of social-payments arrears

text: On various dates in 2001 or 2002, the Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz allowed the applicants' claims against the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) for social-payments arrears.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
A. Proceedings in respect of social-payments arrears

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz ordered that the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) pay the social-payments arrears to the applicants.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
A. Proceedings in respect of social-payments arrears

text: The dates of the judgments and the amounts of the awards in respect of the applicants' social-payments arrears claims are listed in the Annex to the judgment.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants submitted the writs of execution to the Ministry of Finance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Ministry of Finance returned the writs of execution to the applicants on the ground of lack of funds to pay the judgment debts.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The judgments in favour of all the applicants were eventually enforced between September 2004 and April 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 September 2003, the applicants notified the Vladikavkaz Town Administration of their intention to hold a demonstration in Svoboda Square in Vladikavkaz.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The purpose of the planned demonstration in Svoboda Square was to protest against the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department)'s failure to settle the social-payments debt.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The demonstration was scheduled to start on 30 September 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The demonstration was announced as being of unlimited duration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 24 September 2003, the Vladikavkaz Town Administration refused to approve Svoboda Square as the venue for the applicants' demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 24 September 2003, the Vladikavkaz Town Administration suggested that the demonstration be held in front of the Tkhapsayev theatre.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 30 September 2003, the applicants began their demonstration in Svoboda Square in front of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Government building.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: About one hundred people participated in the demonstration in Svoboda Square on 30 September 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The demonstrators put up tents in Svoboda Square and remained in the square day and night.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The demonstrators displayed placards and banners stating their criticisms and demands.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 3 October 2003, the Vladikavkaz Town Legislature annulled the decision of 24 September 2003 at the request of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Vladikavkaz Town Legislature annulled the decision of 24 September 2003 'in connection with a risk of terrorist acts in the places of mass gatherings of people'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Vladikavkaz Town Legislature asked the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) to take measures to break up the demonstration in Svoboda Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Vladikavkaz Town Legislature asked the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) to restore public order in Svoboda Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 11 October 2003, the Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz declared the demonstration in Svoboda Square unlawful because it violated the rights of others.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the demonstration hampered citizens' access to public transport and to the cinema situated in Svoboda Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the demonstration hampered officials' access to the administrative buildings situated in Svoboda Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the chanting of slogans by the applicants disturbed the officials' work.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz noted that the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) had information about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the region.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the mass gathering of people in the vicinity of the administrative buildings in Svoboda Square increased the risk of terrorist acts and other offences being committed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the mass gathering of people in Svoboda Square impeded the conduct of preventive operations by the law-enforcement agencies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz noted that the Vladikavkaz Town Administration had ordered that all meetings and assemblies be held in front of the Tkhapsayev theatre.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the demonstration in Svoboda Square was in breach of the Vladikavkaz Town Administration's order that all meetings and assemblies be held in front of the Tkhapsayev theatre.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that public gatherings of unlimited duration were not authorised by Russian law.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: It appears from a videotape and press articles submitted by the applicants that on 11 October 2003 the police ordered the protesters in Svoboda Square to disperse.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: As the protesters refused to stop the demonstration, the police dismantled the tents the protesters had erected in Svoboda Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: After the police dismantled the tents, the protesters put the tents back up and continued their demonstration in Svoboda Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 18 November 2003, the Supreme Court of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic upheld the judgment of 11 October 2003 of the Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz on appeal.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On 27 November 2003, the Parliament of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic decreed that Svoboda Square in Vladikavkaz was reserved for meetings, assemblies and demonstrations organised at the initiative of the authorities of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic and the town of Vladikavkaz.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: The Parliament of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic decreed that public gatherings other than those organised at the initiative of the authorities were to be held at a venue to be determined by the Vladikavkaz Town Administration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Demonstration organised by the applicants

text: On an unspecified date in December 2003, the protesters ended the demonstration in Svoboda Square.

text: For the relevant provisions of domestic law regarding the enforcement of final judgments, see Burdov v. Russia (no. 2) (application no. 33509/04, §§ 22 and 26-29, 15 January 2009).

Federal Law № 68-ФЗ of 30 April 2010 (in force as of 4 May 2010) provides that in the event of a violation of the right to trial within a reasonable time, Russian citizens are entitled to seek compensation for non-pecuniary damage.

Federal Law № 68-ФЗ of 30 April 2010 (in force as of 4 May 2010) provides that in the event of a violation of the right to enforcement of a final judgment, Russian citizens are entitled to seek compensation for non-pecuniary damage.

Federal Law № 69-ФЗ, adopted on 30 April 2010, introduced pertinent changes in Russian legislation relating to compensation for violations of the right to trial within a reasonable time and the right to enforcement of a final judgment.

Section 6.2 of Federal Law № 68-ФЗ provides that everyone who has an application pending with the European Court of Human Rights concerning a complaint of the nature described in Federal Law № 68-ФЗ has six months to bring the complaint to the domestic courts.
The Russian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of peaceful assembly (Article 31).
The Russian Constitution guarantees the right to hold meetings, demonstrations, marches and pickets (Article 31).

Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992 (in force at the material time) provided that the exercise of the right to freedom of assembly should not violate the rights and freedoms of others (section 1).
Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992 (in force at the material time) prohibited the use of the right to freedom of assembly for the purpose of violently overthrowing the Government (section 1).

Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992 (in force at the material time) prohibited the use of the right to freedom of assembly for the purpose of inciting racial, ethnic or religious hatred (section 1).
Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992 (in force at the material time) prohibited the use of the right to freedom of assembly for the purpose of advocating violence or war (section 1).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 (in force at the material time pursuant to Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992) provided that organisers of an assembly were to serve a written notification on the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly (section 2).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that the notification was to mention the purposes, type, location or itinerary of the assembly, the time of its beginning and end, the expected number of participants, and the names and addresses of the organisers (section 2).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that the municipal authority was to give its response no later than five days before the assembly (section 3).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that the municipal authority could, if necessary, suggest another venue or time for the assembly (section 3).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly could be banned if its purpose was contrary to the Constitution or threatened public order or the security of citizens (section 6).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if no prior notification of the assembly had been given (section 7, case 1).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if a decision banning the assembly had been issued (section 7, case 2).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if the established procedure for the conduct of public assemblies had been breached (section 7, case 3).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if there was a danger to citizens' life or health (section 7, case 4).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if the public order was breached (section 7, case 5).
Succession in Russian law is regulated by Part 3 of the Civil Code.
Under Article 1112 of the Russian Civil Code, succession includes the deceased's property or pecuniary rights or claims.

Under Article 1112 of the Russian Civil Code, succession does not include rights or obligations intrinsically linked to the deceased's person, such as alimony or a right to compensation for damage to health.
Under Articles 1152 and 1162 of the Russian Civil Code, an heir should claim and accept succession and obtain a succession certificate from a public notary.

Under Article 1183 § 1 of the Russian Civil Code, the right to receive salary payments and payments qualifying as such, pension payments and other sums of money payable to the deceased person as a means of subsistence which were not received in his lifetime belongs to the members of the deceased's family who had been residing with him.

Under Article 1183 § 1 of the Russian Civil Code, the right to receive salary payments and payments qualifying as such, pension payments and other sums of money payable to the deceased person as a means of subsistence which were not received in his lifetime also belongs to any disabled dependants, irrespective of their having resided with the deceased or not.

In accordance with section 63 of the Federal Law on Pension Welfare of Military Service Personnel (1993), as in force at the material time, pension payments due to a pensioner but not received in his lifetime are payable to the members of the deceased's family if they were in charge of his or her funeral.

In accordance with section 63 of the Federal Law on Pension Welfare of Military Service Personnel (1993), as in force at the material time, pension payments due to a pensioner but not received in his lifetime shall not be included in the succession.
